---
title: "ecm.sic_split"
description: "Estimated share of Sign-in Canada for each CanadaLogin partner group that replaced it, one row per part and service."
---

How the ECM application Sign-in Canada (`https://auth.id.canada.ca`, since
decommissioned) divides between its CanadaLogin partner groups.

One row is one service in one part. It joins to
[`rp.service`](../rp/service.qmd) on `rp_id`.

`Keywords`: ECM, Sign-in Canada, split, partner group, share, estimate, legacy volume replaced

## Provenance

Each share is an estimate. It is the part's share of CanadaLogin active
credentials in October 2026, taken from the Sign-in Canada credential split. The
table is static and is not refreshed. See the [ECM](../ecm.qmd) page.

* **Updated**: Static
* **Retention**: Indefinitely
* **Steward**: EDCP Data and Research Team
* **Contact**: [Colin Douglas](mailto:colin.douglas@cds-snc.ca)
* **Location**: `s3://canadalogin-reporting-transformed/ecm/sic_split/`

## Fields

| Field Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ecm_service` | `string` | The ECM application being split, as ECM stores its name. |
| `part` | `string` | The partner group, for example `ATIP` or `MyCGC`. |
| `rp_id` | `integer` | The CanadaLogin service in the part. Joins to `rp.service.rp_id`. |
| `part_share` | `float` | The part's estimated share of Sign-in Canada, as a proportion between 0 and 1. |

## Notes

**Sum `part_share` over distinct parts, not over rows.** The value repeats on
every row of a part, so a part with two services counts twice if you sum rows.
ATIP has two services. Take one value per part, then sum:

```sql
SELECT sum(part_share) AS total_share
FROM (
  SELECT part, max(part_share) AS part_share
  FROM ecm.sic_split
  GROUP BY part
)
```

**The shares of the distinct parts add up to 1.** Multiply a part's share by
Sign-in Canada's `active_credentials` in
[`ecm.credential_baseline`](credential_baseline.qmd) to get the part's size.

**The shares are estimates.** They come from CanadaLogin active credentials in
October 2026, not from ECM counts. They stay fixed.
